note: A firm joining the shared hash pool from outside the app: four real curl calls against a local production build, recorded by scripts/public/record-hash-pool-call.ts. A self-serve sandbox key is refused (403) when it tries to register; Brightline Home's own firm key registers, both shown masked. The firm is kept in Remedy's audit ledger, never on the pool row, so a hit names no firm. Only the 64-bit hash and an opaque ref cross. Brightline Home, Fernway Home and their recalls are fictional samples; the photo is the sample charger (Dmitry G, Wikimedia Commons, public domain) and the mug is Kurt Kaiser, CC0.

calls.why: A self-serve sandbox key from the Developers page tries to register the same hash: only a key tied to a connected firm may write to the pool.

error.message: This key can check hashes but not register them. Registering is for firms connected to Remedy, each with a key tied to its firm (scope hash-pool:register), so the shared pool holds only photos a firm has paid on. Request id: req_d4ecbcb675a34ed28531

calls.why: Brightline Home has paid a claim on this photo and registers its hash for its own recall, with its own firm key and opaque ref.

data.note: In the pool. A photo within 4 bits of this hash, sent on any other recall at any firm, is now held for a person.

calls.why: Fernway Home receives the same photo on its own recall and asks the pool with the hash alone.
A photo of a mug, never claimed anywhere, asked the same way: no hit.
